profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record identifies a commercial building at 5635 South Avenue in Boardman, a township adjoining Youngstown in Ohio's Mahoning Valley, tagged as a data center under the name Carrier Services Group. The name points toward telecommunications carrier support work, such as interconnection, switching, or managed network services for other telecom providers, which would be a genuine, if specialized and small scale, category of telecom infrastructure rather than an unrelated business. The Mahoning Valley carries a mix of legacy industrial and telecommunications infrastructure from its manufacturing history, so a facility supporting regional carrier operations in Boardman is plausible on its face. The matching carrierservicesgroup dot com domain does resolve, but it redirects to a bare parking page rather than an active company site describing services, location, or clients, so it could not be used to confirm what actually operates at this address. No independent business registration, press coverage, or alternate operator website could be matched to the name or address. This entry is published as an honest account of what could and could not be confirmed, rather than a guess in either direction, and will be updated if a verifiable operator or business description becomes available.

reading.body:
Carrier Services Group is a facility tagged as telecom data center infrastructure in Boardman, Ohio, within the Youngstown metro area, but no operator website, published specifications, or confirmed business details could be located. The facility's name suggests telecommunications carrier services, consistent with switching, interconnection, or managed services infrastructure serving carrier clients, but the exact scale, ownership, and current purpose remain unconfirmed.

Ohio has 76 mapped data center facilities, of which only 8 publish power capacity figures totaling 60.4 megawatts. This campus does not appear among those eight published figures and therefore ranks outside the state's disclosed capacity, making it invisible to the grid-constrained scaling view that matters for AI infrastructure planning.

Without published specifications, this facility cannot be assessed for relevance to AI compute deployment. Confirmation of ownership, current operation, power capacity, and tenant profile would be required to determine whether Carrier Services Group functions as legacy telecom infrastructure, an active data center serving other industries, or a potential site for AI workload hosting.
